full_judgment:
MM Hossain J: These Rules have been issued in Writ Petition Nos. 1605, 1606, 1682, 1683, 1690, 1763, 1950, 1949, 1950, 1949, 1346, 1181, 1182, 1183, 1319, 1347 and 1348 of 2000 calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why impugned orders shall not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and why Rule 8(1) of Rules, 1998 shall not be declared to be ultra vires of Article 40 of the Constitution and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. In Writ Petition No.1605 of 2000 the petitioner being a citizen of Bangladesh has been engaged in running a Saw Mill for about 11 years with due permission and licence from the concerned authority. He has been doing the business in accordance with law and without violating the terms and conditions of the licence. The respondents, being public servants, are discharging various duties and performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic. In the year 1951 the then government framed Sylhet Forest Transit Rules, 1951 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules, 1951), in exercise of powers conferred by sections 41, 42 and 76 of the Forest Act 1927 (Act XVI of 1927) enforced in the district of Sylhet under Forest (Extension to Sylhet) Act 1950 and in suppression of all previous Rules on the subject. The said Rules have been framed to regulate the transit of all timber or other forest produce within, into or from Sylhet and to establish Saw Mills and Sawpits within the district of Sylhet. Rule 9 of the aforesaid Rules 1951 provides for sanction/ licence to establish Saw Mill or Sawpit within one mile of the cold season bed of any river or channels of the Sylhet district. The elder brother of the petitioner applied tor a licence to the respondent No.1 in 1988 to establish a Saw Mill as per provisions of Sylhet Forest Transit Rules 1951. After completion of formal inquiry the respondent No.1 issued licence in favour of the brother of the petitioner as per Rule 9 of the Sylhet Forest Transit Rules 1951 which was subsequently transferred in the name of the present petitioner in the year 1991 being Licence No. 6150/179 dated 1-12-1991 (AnnexureA). Having obtained the licence the petitioner completed all formalities and set up a Saw Mill on his land and has been continuing the business peacefully without any complaint as to any violation of the terms and conditions of licence and therefore his licence has been renewed by the respondent No.1 upto 30th June, 1999 vide letter dated 29-6-1998 (Annexure B) without any objection from any quarter. In 1998, the respondent No.3, Ministry of Environment and Forest, vide notification SRO No. 270 dated 3-12-1998 framed Sawmills (Licence) Rules, 1998 in exercise of the power conferred by section 41 of the Forest Act, 1927 (hereinafter referred to as the Rules, 1998). The respondent No.1 issued letter dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure D) directing the petitioner to close down his sawmills within 20-2-2000 as per proviso to Rule 8(1) of the Saw-Mills (Licence) Rules, 1998 and intimate the cancellation of operation of the licence NO.6150/179 of 1991 of the petitioner. Thereafter, the petitioner pursued the matter with the concerned authority to get renewal of the licence after recalling the impugned order but yielding no response. The petitioner's licence was renewed upto 30th June, 1999 and thereafter, the respondent No.1 refused to renew the licence on the plea of prohibition under Rule 8(1) of the Rules, 1998. 

 5. In Writ Petition No. 1168 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 vide Memo dated June, 1998 (Annexure B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 10-2-2000 (Annexure E). In Writ Petition No. 1181 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th May, 1999 vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-A-1) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No. 1182 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-A-1) and the petitioner's licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1183 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-A-1) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1319 of 2000 petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-A-1) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure D). In Writ Petition No.1346 of 2000 petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1998 vide Memo dated 1st July, 1997 (Annexure C) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 10-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1347 of 2000 petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 vide Memo dated 15th July, 1998 (Annexure C) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 9-2-2000 (Annexure E). In Writ Petition NO.1348 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1998 (Annexure A) vide Memo dated 11th June, 1996 (Annexure C) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 10-2-2000 (Annexure D). In Writ Petition No.1529, of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 (Annexure-A) vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 10-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1606 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 Annexure-A) vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1682 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 (Annexure-A) vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 ' (Annexure-B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000(Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1683 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 Annexure-A) vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1690 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 (Annexure-A) vide Memo dated 12th May, 1998 (Annexure-B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000(Annexure-D). In Writ Petition No.1763 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30'h June, 1999 Annexure-A) vide Memo dated 30th June, 1998 (Annexure-B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure-D). In Writ Petition NO.1949 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 (Annexure-A) vide Memo dated 30th June, 1997 (Annexure-B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated ,14-2-2000 (AnnexureD). In Writ Petition No.1950 of 2000 the petitioner's licence was finally renewed till 30th June, 1999 (AnnexureA) vide Memo dated 30th June, 1997 (Annexure B) and the licence was cancelled by the impugned order dated 14-2-2000 (Annexure D). In all these matters the impugned orders were issued in identical terms and the respective petitioners obtained these Rules in identical terms. Since all these Rules are taken up together for hearing the respondent government filed Affidavit-in- Opposition in Writ Petition No.1348 and prayed to accept the said Affidavit-in-Opposition against all the remaining Rules. 

 8. Mr Fida M Kamal, the learned Additional Attorney-General, for the respondents in all these Rules. submits that the writ petitions are not maintainable in view of the promulgation of Saw-Mills (Licence) Rules, 1998 in exercise of the powers conferred by section 41 of the Forest Act, 1927 which has been made applicable for the whole territory of Bangladesh. He then submits that section 41 of the Forest Act, 1927 as amended by the Forest (Amendment) Act 1990 empowers the government to frame Rules to regulate the transit by land or water of timbers or other forest produces, and, in particular, such Rules apply absolutely or subject to conditions within specified local limits, the establishment of wood-based industries including saw-mills, sawpits, furniture marts and brickfields, etc and, as such, framing of the Saw-Mills (Licence) Rules, 1998 under section 41 of the Forest Act 1927 (as amended) has been made with lawful authority. He submits that Forest Act 1927 being a comprehensive Act has been extended to the District of Sylhet by the Forest (Extension to Sylhet) Act, 1950 and all the Rules framed thereunder and that the Assam Forest Regulations 1891 applicable to the district of Sylhet has been repealed. The learned Additional Attorney-General submits that the Rule making powers under section 41 of the Forest Act 1927 (as amended) empowers the government to frame rules for the whole territory of the republic including the greater District of Sylhet which is now a Division consisting of the districts of Habigonj, Sunamgonj, Moulvibazar and Sylhet. The learned Additional Attorney General further submits that the respondent No. 2 issued the impugned orders upon the petitioners, to close down their saw-mills within 180 days because of the contravention of the provisions of Rule 8 of the Rules of 1998, having given them sufficient opportunity to defend themselves and thereby the respondent No. 2 complied with the principles of natural justice and, as such, there being no illegality in. the impugned orders the Rules are liable to be discharged. He then submits that the government having been empowered under section 41 of the Forest Act, 1927 framed Saw-Mills (Licence) Rules, 1998 without affecting the petitioner's fundamental rights as the said Rules are reasonable and, as such, the question of ultra vires does not arise. He contends that the Rules of 1998 having been framed in accordance with law, the same cannot be declared to be ultra vires to the Constitution nor to have been issued in colourable exercise of the executive authority and that the same stands valid and there is no question of challenging the vires of the Rules, 1998 and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. He finally submits that having regard to the monopoly use of timbers in the neighbouring villages of the reserved or vested forests and international land border areas, the people became very much interested to establish saw-mills though quantity of timbers and forest produces in Sylhet Division are so meagre as not to cope with the demands of saw-mills and in the circumstances to preserve and protect the forests from theft and pilferage, the Rules of 1998 have been framed with reasonable restriction in the public interest and, as such, there is no question of ultra vires to the provisions of the Constitution. He finally submits that the impugned orders have been issued as per provisions of Rule 8(1) of the aforesaid Rules of 1998 to protect the smuggling of timbers and forest produces from across the international land border and accordingly, uniform Rules have been promulgated for the whole territory of the Republic for the greater interest of the nation and, as such, the Saw-Mills (Licence) Rules, 1998 have been made with lawful authority and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 10. It should be mentioned that the Forest Act 1927 has been extended to the District of Sylhet by the Forest (Extension to Sylhet) Act, 1950 on 29th March 1950 by the then East Bengal Act No. XI of 1950.
